correctness.rationale: Boundary inner unimodularity makes every even Hardy moment a finite binomial pairing. For cross indices j>k, the test polynomial q^k has degree at most kn <= (m-1)n, proving dependence on that finite Taylor jet without approximation. Coercivity, strict convexity and injectivity prove existence/uniqueness. The classical inverse Schur recursion supplies a finite Blaschke jet interpolant of degree <= (m-1)n+1. Comparing z^L and -z^L at q=1+z^n proves an exact -4m objective gap for m>=2,n>=1; z^(L+1) forces any matching Blaschke product to have degree >= L+1. The packaged standalone program compares the finite identity with independent circle integration in three nontrivial cases and tests exact sharpness integers in four, but finite tests are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: Finite-degree approximation in H^(2m) to the reciprocal of an arbitrary inner function is a natural nonlinear problem; the entire objective is exactly compressed to the first (m-1)n+1 coefficients, and every such problem has a finite Blaschke representative of optimal universal degree (m-1)n+1. Both cutoffs are sharp and independent of whether the inner generator is infinite/singular. These exact model-complexity invariants support finite algebraic optimization and comparison of nonidentical inner functions without claiming general root formulas. The result goes beyond one-case H4 calculations and beyond the known m=1 Hilbert degeneration.
